title: Prismor Policy Schema
description: Schema for Prismor YAML policy files that define detection rules, allowlists, and enforcement actions.

rules.description: Detection rules evaluated against agent events

allowlists.description: Allowlist entries that suppress specific rule matches

settings.description: Policy-level settings that control enforcement behaviour

default_mode.description: Global observe/enforce default for rules that don't set their own `mode`. Defaults to observe (nothing blocks until a rule is flipped to enforce).

selection.description: `explicit` means the rules listed in this file are the complete blocking set, as chosen rule by rule in `prismor setup`. A safety-floor rule that is not listed reports instead of blocking. Honored only for a locally-authored policy on an unmanaged workspace — it is ignored from a signed org bundle, and never applies to Prismor's self-protection rules.
selection.$comment: Opt-in floor. The floor is otherwise unconditional, so this is deliberately not something an org policy can set.

block_categories.description: Legacy: finding categories eligible to block. Enforcement is now decided per-rule via `mode`/`default_mode`; this is retained for compatibility.

manifest_patterns.description: Regex patterns that identify dependency manifest files (used for severity upgrades)

egress_allowlist.description: DEPRECATED, superseded by `egress`. Outbound domains allowed without a warning (supports wildcards, e.g. "*.github.com"). Empty allows all. Never blocks.

mcp_transport_action.description: Action for insecure MCP remote-transport findings raised by scan (cleartext/raw-IP/off-allowlist/hardcoded-secret). Defaults to warn.

semantic_guard.description: Settings for the optional LLM-assisted semantic prompt-injection layer.

sandbox.description: Docker-backed shell sandbox settings for constraining allowed Bash commands.

enabled.description: Whether hook-dispatch rewrites supported Bash tool calls through the sandbox runner.

backend.description: Sandbox backend. Docker is the v1 backend.

mode.description: observe logs unavailable sandbox state; enforce fails closed when the sandbox is unavailable.

image.description: Container image used for sandboxed shell execution.

workdir.description: Container working directory for the workspace mount.

network.description: Docker network mode. allowlist currently fails closed to none because Docker cannot enforce domain allowlists by itself.

workspace_mount.description: Whether the workspace bind mount is read-only or read-write.

read_only_root.description: Run the container with a read-only root filesystem.

tmpfs.description: Docker --tmpfs entries for controlled writable scratch space.

env_allowlist.description: Host environment variable names allowed into the sandbox.

agent_controls.description: Org-pushed per-agent controls, keyed by agent instance name (the adapter's name=) or framework id for unnamed agents. Served only in the signed remote policy; merged tighten-only with the local agents.yaml (an org kill-switch cannot be re-enabled locally).

enabled.description: false = kill switch: every tool call from this agent blocks

mode.description: Forced mode override for this agent

iam_profile.description: IAM profile to enforce (must be defined in the local/project iam.yaml)

prompt_guardrails.description: Operator-written instructions added to the agent's context at session start and when they change (see guardrails.py). Advice the model reads, not enforcement.

agents.description: Keyed by agent name or framework id; "*" applies to every agent.

sessions.description: Per-session tuning keyed by session id.

rule_exemptions.description: Admin-granted per-event rule exemptions, matched at eval time against the current user/device/session. 'allow' drops the finding; 'flag' downgrades it to a non-blocking warning. Core/floor rules can never be exempted.

expires.description: ISO-8601 expiry; absent = permanent until revoked

egress.description: Policy-driven network egress control. Screens every network event and shell command destination (URLs of any scheme, user@host:path, bare curl/wget hosts, nc/telnet host+port) against allow/deny lists.

enabled.description: Opt in to egress screening. Defaults to false.

mode.description: observe logs only; enforce blocks the call. Org-signed enforce is authoritative and survives a local observe downgrade.

default.description: Verdict for a destination no entry matches. `deny` makes `allow` a strict allowlist.

allow_private.description: Skip the check for loopback/RFC1918/link-local/.local destinations. Cloud metadata endpoints are never treated as private. Defaults to true.

deny.description: Destinations refused. Evaluated before `allow`, so an explicit deny always wins.

agents.description: Per-agent overrides keyed by registered agent name, layered over the fleet lists.

data_boundary.description: Data boundary: screens what an outbound call SENDS (emails, phones, cards, secrets, files) against where it is going (internal / trusted / external / untrusted). Catches agents that follow third-party docs into shipping the user's own data to a service the user never approved, while letting synthetic/test payloads and trusted destinations through silently.

mode.description: observe logs only; enforce honors step_up/redact/block. observe/warn class actions never block regardless.

trusted_domains.description: Hosts (glob `*.corp.com`, IP, CIDR) that may receive any class silently. VCS hosts and package registries are trusted by default.

classes.description: Per data class, the action per destination tier. Classes: email, phone, ssn, card, iban, secret (non-vendor destinations only), file (uploads).

per_domain.description: Per-host carve-outs by class, e.g. `api.resend.com: {email: allow}`.

bulk_threshold.description: Distinct values of one class in a single call at/above which the action escalates one rung. Default 10.

self_identity.description: Emails/phones that identify the user; sending them externally escalates one rung. git user.email and enrolment email are added automatically unless self_identity_auto is false.

self_identity_auto.description: Discover the user's own email from git config / enrolment. Default true.

unknown_cli.description: Posture for a CLI whose destination cannot be inferred from argv. Default observe. Escalated to the external tier automatically when the binary was installed this session or a doc from that vendor was just fetched.

egressEntry.description: A destination matcher: either a bare host string or an object with additional constraints.

oneOf.description: Hostname, wildcard ("*.github.com"), "*", IP address, or CIDR.

host.description: Hostname, wildcard ("*.github.com"), "*", IP address, or CIDR ("10.0.0.0/8").

ports.description: Restrict this entry to these destination ports.

schemes.description: Restrict this entry to these URL schemes (https, ssh, postgres, …).

agents.description: Restrict this entry to these registered agent names.

action.description: Override the verdict for this entry. Defaults to the list it appears in.

reason.description: Human-readable justification, surfaced in the finding.

severity.description: Finding severity when this rule matches

category.description: Finding category for grouping and feed correlation

event_types.description: Event types this rule applies to (shell, file_read, file_write, network, prompt, tool_result, memory, skill_manifest, ui_action, mcp). A rule listing tool_result is automatically applied to memory (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md) content too. The 'mcp' alias matches any MCP tool call regardless of whether it classifies as a remote (network) or local stdio (tool_result) event. 'ui_action' is a GUI agent operating an on-screen control (click, key press, typed text) rather than running a command or touching a file.

fields.description: Event fields to match against. Defaults to the canonical field for the event type (command for shell, path for file_*, url for network, combined_text for prompt/tool_result, control_label for ui_action, tool_name for the mcp alias). For MCP guardrails: tool_name is the full mcp__server__tool tag, mcp_server / mcp_tool are the parsed parts, mcp_args is the serialized pre-call arguments regardless of transport, and outbound_payload is the remote-transport raw form of the same. For GUI guardrails (ui_action): control_label is the target control's accessibility label, ax_role its accessibility role, app_name the owning application, and typed_text the text about to be committed.

patterns.description: Regex patterns (Python re syntax). A match on ANY pattern triggers the rule.

action.description: Authorization verdict when this rule fires as an enforce finding on a pre-action event. block = deny; step_up = require inline human approval (maps to an 'ask' prompt on Claude/Copilot; other surfaces fail closed); modify = rewrite the tool input via `transform`; defer = escalate to the semantic evaluator. warn/log are non-blocking (observe). Whether a rule blocks at all is still gated by `mode`/`default_mode`.

transform.description: Named input transform applied when action is 'modify'. The hook dispatcher rewrites the tool input via this transform.

mode.description: Per-rule observe/enforce override. observe = detect + log only; enforce = block on a pre-action event. Omit to inherit settings.default_mode (default observe).

add_patterns.description: Extra regex patterns to add to this rule on top of its defaults. Custom org-specific detections — strengthen-only.

disable_patterns.description: Default regex patterns to disable for this rule, referenced by their exact regex string. Not allowed on core protections. A no-match entry is ignored (drift fails toward more detection).

enabled.description: Whether this rule is active. Defaults to true.

severity_on_write.description: Override severity when the matched event_type is file_write

severity_on_manifest.description: Override severity when the matched path is a dependency manifest file

pattern_groups.description: Named groups of regex patterns, referenced by name from `condition`. Ignored unless `condition` is also set. The rule's own `patterns` list is always addressable as the group name `patterns`.

condition.description: Optional boolean expression over pattern-group names, e.g. "patterns and not benign_context" or "2 of (curl_use, env_read, base64_encode)". Supports and/or/not, parentheses, and 'any of'/'all of'/'N of' quantifiers. When omitted the rule fires if ANY pattern matches (the default). Ignored on core protections, which cannot be narrowed.

rule_ids.description: Rule IDs this allowlist applies to. Use ['*'] for all rules.

patterns.description: Regex patterns that, when matched, suppress the finding.

type.description: allow (default) suppresses a matching finding. veto does the opposite and wins: a matching veto disqualifies every allowlist from suppressing that finding, so a broad exception can be carved back without making its patterns brittle. Vetoes are resolved before any allow, independent of entry order.
type.$comment: A field on the entry rather than a separate section: a veto is scoped by rule_ids and matched by patterns exactly like an allow, and sharing the shape keeps both halves of a carve-out in one list.

reason.description: Human-readable reason for this allowlist entry

expires.description: Optional ISO-8601 timestamp after which this entry stops applying, so a temporary exception (`prismor allow --expires 30m`) lapses instead of quietly becoming permanent policy.
